summary: Extended the client-completion probe and requested a fresh execution. The harness now continues past the observed re-queue: it passes the re-queued proposal to the replica's own handlePropose path (creating instance (0,1)), completes that instance's pre-accept exchange, and calls the package's own execution entry point so the client reply is measured rather than derived. Local native feedback shows the whole protection chain working: the replacement decision at instance (0,0) re-queued the pending request (command id 77), the re-proposed instance (0,1) was decided, execution returned true with 17 reply bytes, and the decoded reply carries command id 77 with ok 1 - so the client's request completes end-to-end after the recovery replaced it. The successor experiment records the revision reason, the added execution-path source range and prerequisite chain, and a new comparison asserting that the completion reply carries the same command id, alongside the unchanged re-queue comparison. Its receipt and the corresponding interpretation update remain outstanding, as does the explicit answer to the reply-side gap registered last turn (which this revision is designed to close by measurement).
